name: Bounti
subcategory: AI account research and outreach drafting
tagline: An AI go-to-market teammate that researches target accounts and drafts personalized outreach for sales and marketing teams.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The visible core is a research loop: take a company and a person, crawl their public footprint, summarize what matters, then draft an opener that references it. An agent can build that in a sitting with a search API, a scraper, and an LLM, and for one person working a list of fifty accounts it will be fine. The gaps are everything around the loop: enrichment data that is actually current, contact discovery, CRM writeback, sequencing, and inbox deliverability, which is a whole separate discipline you do not want to learn by accident. Quality also drifts fast without someone tuning prompts against reply data you do not have. Call it a weekend build that covers the research half and punts on the send half.
coreLoopDIY: Takes a list of company domains and contact names, crawls public pages and search results, and writes a research brief plus a drafted first-touch email per account into files and a local database.
requirements: A web search API key (Tavily, Brave, or similar)
A list of target companies you already have
whatYouLose: Contact and firmographic enrichment: you get whatever the open web gives you, not a maintained database
CRM sync, so every brief lives in your folder and nowhere your pipeline can see it
Sending infrastructure, warmup, and deliverability monitoring
Sequencing, reply detection, and follow-up logic
Prompt quality tuned against real reply rates across many customers
moatNotes: The research prompt is the easy part. Fresh, deduped account and contact data plus CRM plumbing is the part that costs money every month.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because a sales team is not paying for a research script, they are paying for briefs that land in the CRM next to the right record, contacts that are still employed, and email that reaches the inbox. A personal build gets you good drafts for accounts you already know about, which is genuinely useful if you are a founder doing your own outbound. It stops being useful the moment two people need to work the same list, or the moment your homemade sender torches your domain reputation.
notes: Fine for founder-led outbound on a short list; do not point it at your main sending domain.
prompt:
Build a local CLI tool called "scout" that researches target accounts and drafts first-touch outreach.

Stack, no substitutions: TypeScript on Node 20, commander for the CLI, better-sqlite3 for storage, undici for fetch, cheerio for HTML parsing, zod for config validation. No web UI, no server, no accounts, no telemetry.

Inputs: a CSV at ./targets.csv with columns company,domain,contact_name,contact_title,notes. Secrets in .env: LLM_API_KEY, SEARCH_API_KEY. Read them with dotenv and fail loudly with a clear message if missing.

Pipeline per row, all steps cached in SQLite so reruns are cheap:
1. Crawl the domain: fetch homepage plus up to 6 internal pages matching /about, /product, /pricing, /customers, /careers, /blog. Respect robots.txt, 1 request per second per host, 10s timeout, skip on error and record why.
2. Strip to readable text with cheerio, cap at 4000 tokens per page.
3. Run 3 web searches via the search API: "{company} funding", "{company} news", "{contact_name} {company}". Store top 5 results with snippets.
4. Call the LLM once to produce a structured brief: what the company does, who they sell to, 3 recent signals with source URLs, 2 plausible pain hypotheses, and a confidence note where evidence is thin.
5. Call the LLM again to draft one outreach email: max 90 words, one specific reference to a cited signal, one clear ask, no flattery, no "I hope this finds you well". Also produce a 2-line LinkedIn version.
6. Require every factual claim in the brief to carry a source URL. Drop unsourced claims rather than keeping them.

Output: ./out/{domain}.md containing brief, sources, email draft, and a token cost line. Also a summary table printed to stdout with per-row status.

Commands: scout run [--limit n] [--force], scout show domain, scout export --csv.

Explicitly out of scope, do not build: sending email, SMTP or Gmail auth, CRM integration, contact discovery or email guessing, follow-up sequencing, any hosted dashboard.

Include a README with setup in 5 steps, a targets.csv.example, and vitest tests for the CSV parser, the robots check, and the cache layer. Handle rate limits with exponential backoff and make every LLM call retry twice before giving up.
